title: Phantom Types for Safe IDs & Units
hints: A generic parameter can be a compile-time tag that's never stored.
`Length<Unit>` stores only a `Double`; `+` is only defined for two lengths with the same `Unit`.
jsBridge: A phantom type parameter (`Length<Meters>`) exists only at compile time, so mixing meters and feet is a type error. TS approximates this with branded types (`number & {__brand: 'm'}`). Swift's version is first-class and free at runtime.

compass.q: TS branded types need casts to create. What makes Swift phantom types more ergonomic?
Phantom types vs Foundation's `Measurement<UnitLength>`: when would you use each?
Can `Length<Meters>` and `Length<Feet>` be added accidentally? What about through `Any`?
`Tagged<User, UUID>` IDs (Point-Free's swift-tagged) prevent passing a `PostID` where a `UserID` is expected. Worth it in your app?
